explain.say: June 1816, by Lake Geneva. Rain for days, and Byron challenges his friends to write ghost stories. Eighteen-year-old Mary Shelley imagines a scientist kneeling beside a thing he has made. Look at the board: her novel is built like an onion, stories inside stories.

explain.say: The outer layer: Robert Walton, an explorer in the Arctic, writes letters to his sister. He rescues Victor Frankenstein from the ice. Inside, Victor tells how ambition drove him to give life to a body, then flee from it. The subtitle is The Modern Prometheus, the Titan who stole fire. Why begin with Walton?

explain.say: The heart of the onion is the Creature's own tale. Look at his panels. He learns to read by secretly watching the De Lacey family, and even reads Paradise Lost. When he shows himself, they flee in terror. The novel's epigraph asks the maker: did I request thee, Maker, from my clay to mould me man? How would you feel?

explain.say: A gentle warning: violence follows. He asks Victor for a companion and promises to vanish. Victor starts, then tears the mate apart. In revenge the Creature kills Victor's brother, his best friend and his bride. Look at the fifth panel. Who is responsible?

explain.say: Victor dies chasing him across the ice, and the Creature mourns and drifts into the dark. On the left, a warning about science without limits. On the right, a child abandoned and made cruel; Ellen Moers read it as a myth of birth. Brilliant. Challenge: decide who is the real monster.

faq.q: Why is Frankenstein told through several narrators?
faq.a: The frame lets us hear Walton, Victor and the Creature in turn, so we judge each against the others. It also lets the Creature speak for himself at the very centre.

faq.q: What does The Modern Prometheus mean?
faq.a: In Greek myth Prometheus stole fire from the gods for humans and was punished. Victor similarly seizes the power to create life and suffers for it.

faq.q: Why does the Creature turn violent?
faq.a: He begins gentle and eager for love, but everyone, starting with his creator, rejects him for his appearance. Lonely and refused a companion, he turns to revenge.

faq.q: Is Frankenstein the name of the monster?
faq.a: No. Victor Frankenstein is the scientist. His creation has no name and is called the creature, the daemon, the wretch and other names.

faq.q: How did Mary Shelley come to write Frankenstein?
faq.a: During a ghost-story contest at the Villa Diodati in June 1816, she imagined a scientist and his creation in a waking dream, and expanded it into a novel published in 1818.

facts: Frankenstein was first published anonymously on 1 January 1818.
Mary Shelley was eighteen when she began the story in 1816.
Her revised 1831 edition added an introduction describing how the story came to her.
